title: SQL injection
guidance: SQL syntax and untrusted values must remain separate. Use the database driver's bound parameter API, preserve the original query's intent, and allowlist any dynamic identifiers. A syntactic match does not establish attacker control or reachability.

title: OS command injection
guidance: Avoid shell interpretation. Prefer a dedicated library or a fixed executable with an argument list and shell disabled. Validate arguments and consider option injection and path restrictions. Confirm whether untrusted data reaches the command.

title: Code injection through eval
guidance: Do not evaluate input as executable code. For a JSON-only contract use JSON.parse or json.loads and validate the resulting schema. This changes behavior if callers rely on arbitrary expressions; require compatibility tests.

title: Cross-site scripting
guidance: Prefer textContent when rendering text. When HTML is required, apply an approved sanitization library and contextual encoding. Determine input provenance and whether the rendering context is attacker controlled.

title: Certificate verification
guidance: Require certificate and hostname verification. Configure a trusted certificate authority rather than disabling verification. Test valid, expired, untrusted, and wrong-host certificates.

title: Unsafe deserialization
guidance: Use a data-only serialization format. For YAML use yaml.safe_load and schema validation. Never deserialize untrusted Python pickle data. Confirm whether custom object construction is an application requirement.

title: Hardcoded credentials
guidance: Treat suspected credential values as sensitive. Verify validity without copying them into chats or reports. Revoke active credentials, rotate consumers, and use a managed secret store. Removing a value from a file does not revoke it or remove it from history.

title: Risky cryptographic algorithm
guidance: Distinguish security-sensitive cryptography from non-security checksums. Prefer current vetted algorithms and dedicated password hashing libraries. Review interoperability and migration requirements before changing stored representations.
